sermon.title: Identifying an Apostle
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In session one on ministry gifts, Pastor David G. Kincer explains that apostles are a job description set by God, not a title. He shows how Jesus made the twelve, gave them power and authority, and sent them without pay; how even they had flaws until three possessions changed them—opened understanding, the Holy Ghost, and love; and the biblical signs of an apostle.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Several phrases not clear (21:00, 24:20, 31:30, 33:40, 41:30). He cites Luke 7:5 for “increase our faith” (Luke 17:5), 2 Corinthians 5:11 for “the love of Christ compels us” (5:14), Acts 17:5 for “turned the world upside down” (17:6), and says “Ephesians” for the fruit of the Spirit. Unchecked: Chinese Communist Party ~7% (80–100 million) and almost 200 million Christians in China. Sensitive content kept as spoken: Catholic Dark Ages corruption, missionaries and indigenous dress, Second Amendment in the Bible, capitalism vs. socialism/communism, Oral Roberts and Liberty universities named, Peter’s profanity.

chunks.section_question: Does God working through someone prove they are holy?
chunks.short_answer: They went out preaching and healing everywhere—including Judas, the thief. Because God does something through an impure vessel doesn’t make it pure. In Mark 6:30 they reported back to Jesus—the safest thing to do—with no financial complaints.

chunks.section_question: Do we need miracles or marketing to draw crowds?

faqs.question: Can a university make you an apostle?
faqs.answer: No—only God sets people in the church.

faqs.question: Does the church need many apostles?
faqs.answer: No—only a few, but it needs many helpers, administrators, prayers and worshipers.

faqs.question: What is the kingdom of heaven?
faqs.answer: An area ruled over by a king, and the King is Jesus Christ.

faqs.question: Should ministers live richly off the people?
faqs.answer: He contrasts Jesus sending them without pay with ministers driving Rolls-Royces while widows give.

faqs.question: Is the word as powerful as miracles?
faqs.answer: Yes—John the Baptist drew the same crowds without any miracle.

faqs.question: Can Christians use profanity?
faqs.answer: He says no—just because the secular world talks that way doesn’t mean we can.

faqs.question: Why does doctrine matter?
faqs.answer: Doctrine shapes your behavior; it is not innocent.

faqs.question: Is he at war with other churches?
faqs.answer: No—he may disagree with them, but his battle is with sin and principalities and powers.

faqs.question: What does the home need from a father?
faqs.answer: Love—not tongues and prophesying through the house, but a father who plays ball with his kids.
